area.scope.heading: The same repair costs differently in a condo, a cottage and a row house
area.scope.1.why: In the Old Town Triangle District, work that changes the outside, like a new condenser in view, can need Landmarks review.
area.scope.2.why: Row houses on Crilly Court and Eugenie can still run boilers and radiators; rehabbed cottages mostly run furnaces.
area.scope.3.why: Condensers for Old Town condos sit on shared roofs, so the association's access rules shape the visit.
area.scope.4.why: Cottages built after the 1871 fire have low basements and narrow gangways, which set how equipment comes in and out.
area.scope.5.why: Kitchens on Wells run exhaust hoods and make-up air with the rooftop units, so work is booked around service hours.
area.scope.6.why: The biggest swing of all. Where the unit has years left, we say so.

area.buildings.heading: What heats and cools your Old Town building
area.buildings.1.title: Condo building
area.buildings.1.body: A furnace or heat pump per unit, with the condenser on the roof. The association sets the rules for roof work.
area.buildings.2.title: Worker's cottage
area.buildings.2.body: A basement furnace or a small boiler, often rehabbed. Low basements and narrow gangways set the access.
area.buildings.3.title: Victorian row house
area.buildings.3.body: Often a boiler and radiators, sometimes converted to forced air. Ductless is a common way to cool.
area.buildings.4.title: Restaurant or bar
area.buildings.4.body: Rooftop units with kitchen exhaust and make-up air. Work is scheduled around service hours.

area.faq.heading: Old Town HVAC, answered
area.faq.1.q: Can the boiler in my row house be repaired, or does it need replacing?
area.faq.1.a: Often it can be repaired. We diagnose first, and where the boiler has years left, we say so. Replacement is quoted only when the repair stops making sense.
area.faq.2.q: How far is your shop from Old Town?
area.faq.3.q: Does HVAC work in the Old Town Triangle need Landmarks approval?
area.faq.4.q: Does HVAC repair in Chicago need a permit?
area.cta.body: Have the make of your furnace, boiler or condenser to hand, and tell us what it's doing. In a condo building, mention who lets us onto the roof.

extras.faq.2.a: Under a mile. The shop is at 1225 N Cleaver St, south-west of the corner at North Ave and Halsted, and Rob runs the calls from there.
extras.faq.3.a: Repairs inside the house don't. Work that changes the outside, like a new condenser in view of the street, can need Landmarks review first.
extras.faq.4.a: No. Chicago doesn't require a permit to repair, diagnose or maintain heating and cooling. Permits cover installs and construction, so a company's permit count says little about its repair work.

_sources.boundaries: City of Chicago neighborhood polygon 'Old Town' (y6yq-dbs2): Armitage (north), Division (south), Halsted north of North Ave and Clybourn / Larrabee south of it (west), Clark north of North Ave and LaSalle south of it (east). The Better Vacation's Old Town guide gives the same lines: Division, Armitage, Halsted and Clybourn, Clark. Old Town has no legal boundary (Wikipedia). The Old Town Triangle, north of North Ave, is in Lincoln Park (7), which has its own page; the rest is Near North Side (8).
_sources.districts: Wikipedia (Old Town, Chicago): Old Town Triangle (Clark, North, Ogden), Wells Street, The Second City at 1616 N Wells; Old Town Triangle District, Chicago Landmark 1977. Sun-Times and Grotto Network guides: Wells as the commercial strip, the Sedgwick Brown Line stop at North Ave.
_sources.buildings: Frommer's walking tour and Crib Chatter (1712 N Crilly): Crilly Court 1885 row houses; Olsen-Hansen row houses on Eugenie (1886); Menomonee Street worker's cottages; Chicago Landmarks (Martin Schnitzius Cottage): post-1871 frame cottages built outside the fire limits. Condos, townhomes and restaurants: the area permit mix (ductwork 8, rooftop units 4, kitchen exhaust 4, furnace 4).
